clue.text: False pride: it resolves current disruption

indicators.note: something false is not genuine, so the next word is not to be read as it stands
to resolve can mean to break up into parts, so the preceding words are broken down and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A moralising maxim: false pride is the thing that settles a disrupted state of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide rip is a stretch of rough, turbulent water where opposing flows meet, a disturbance in the sea's movement.

clue.text: Dialectal distinction within the dynasty

indicators.note: one item placed in another is enclosed by it, so the letter goes inside the dynasty's name

parts.note: the T'ang dynasty ruled China from the 7th to 10th centuries
W is a standard abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A historian notes a regional quirk of speech found within a ruling Chinese house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' reads as one word but splits into with (W) and in, the instruction to place it inside TANG, giving TWANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal regional accent, the sort of feature that marks out one local speech from another.

clue.text: Muck-spreaders find it entrancing

parts.note: surface reading: farmers spreading manure are enchanted by something
setter's reading: people with muddy boots meet this mat at the entrance of a house

explanation.walkthrough: Entrancing is read as at the entrance: the mat where visitors wipe muddy feet lies by the front door.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat lies at a house's threshold, where callers with dirty shoes scrape off mud before stepping inside.

clue.text: Degenerate English teaching by this

parts.note: to rot is to decay or degenerate
E is the usual abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A complaint that English teaching has gone downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degenerate' looks like an adjective on English but is a verb giving ROT; the definition relies on the phrase teaching by rote.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning by rote means memorising through mechanical repetition, a method of instruction long criticised in schools.

clue.text: The 24 21 for one: Will happy with it; a-any dissension?

indicators.note: dissension is disagreement and disorder, so the letters fall out of their given order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
the stammered a-any supplies both letters

explanation.surface: Is Shakespeare content with his inset drama, or does anyone object? The stammer suggests a nervous questioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 and 21 together are MOUSETRAP: The Mousetrap is the play Hamlet stages before Claudius. Will is Shakespeare in the surface, but just four letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hamlet, The Mousetrap is a drama performed by players inside the main drama, the classic example of the device.

clue.text: Say, shall we inform the President? This guy could build bridges!

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the phrase and listen to how it comes out

parts.note: to inform is to tell, and Gerald Ford was a US President

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to brief the President, then praises a man able to build bridges, in the diplomatic sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Telford was the Scottish civil engineer behind the Menai Suspension Bridge; 'build bridges' sounds like peacemaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Telford was a great Scottish civil engineer whose works include many famous bridges, aqueducts and canals.

clue.text: Macbeth, Act 1: "Thesps" hotly disposed

indicators.note: disposed means arranged or set out, so these letters are laid out afresh

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stage notes for the opening act of Macbeth, with excitable actors keen to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: Actors avoid naming Macbeth in a theatre for superstition, calling it by this euphemism instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Superstitious actors refer to Shakespeare's tragedy set in Scotland by this nickname rather than speaking its title backstage.

clue.text: Flavouring's a sour disappointment when added to the pot

indicators.note: one thing added to another sits next to it, so the two pieces join end to end

parts.note: a lemon is a dud, and the fruit is sour
pot and grass are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A cook's lament: a seasoning that turns sour when put into the saucepan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' suggests a cooking vessel in a kitchen surface, but here it is the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon grass is a tropical herb with a citrus aroma, widely used to season Thai and Vietnamese cooking.

clue.text: Talon torn from goldfinch

indicators.note: something torn is ripped apart, so the claw's letters are pulled out of order

parts.note: taken as written
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A claw ripped from a small yellow songbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goldfinch' must be split: gold gives the heraldic OR and finch is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European songbird, a bunting, loosely grouped with finches and once eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Mates with this look to make Bucks Fizz?

definitions.text: Mates with this look to make Bucks Fizz?

parts.words: Mates with this look to make Bucks Fizz?
parts.note: surface reading: friends mixing a cocktail of champagne and orange juice

parts.words: Mates with this look to make Bucks Fizz?
parts.note: setter's reading: female deer with soft, wide gazes set the males excited

explanation.walkthrough: Buck's fizz is a British champagne and orange cocktail; here bucks are male deer, and their mates are does with gentle, wide eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Having large, innocent, appealing eyes like a female deer's is what describing someone this way means.

clue.text: Re-dial with a change of heart

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: Someone redials a number after changing their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Re-dial' looks like one verb, but it splits into re and dial.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-face is a complete reversal of opinion or policy, originally a military turn to face the opposite way.

clue.text: See dignity in this joint

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the tall headdress marking a bishop's office, a see being a bishop's diocese
second meaning: a corner joint where two pieces meet at an angle

explanation.surface: Spot some grandeur in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not the verb but a bishop's diocese, whose dignity is symbolised by the bishop's headdress.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is both a bishop's ceremonial headgear and a carpentry joint made by bevelling two ends to meet at an angle.

clue.text: See 12

definitions.note: a pointer: the definition, Measure for Measure, is in the clue at 12

wordplay.note: the clue at 12, whose rearranged letters supply the end of the saying

explanation.walkthrough: This light ends 12-across: TWO CAN PLAY (12) AT THAT (14) GAME (11), the saying defined there by Measure for Measure.
explanation.definitionFit: The final word of the proverb about retaliation in kind, meaning a contest or sport someone else has started.

clue.text: (and 14, 11) "Measure for Measure" offered without a second to placate my angst. What a mess!

definitions.note: defines the whole phrase across 12, 14 and 11

indicators.note: a mess is a disorderly muddle, so the letters before it are scrambled
without means lacking, so the letter is dropped from the jumble

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the exclamation itself joining the mix
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Someone offers Shakespeare's comedy to calm their worries, then despairs at the chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase TWO CAN PLAY AT THAT GAME spans 12, 14 and 11. 'What a' does double duty; remove one S from all the letters before 'mess', then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Measure for measure means retaliation in kind, tit for tat, which is the threat this saying makes.

clue.text: The driver of Blake's fire appliance?

definitions.text: The driver of Blake's fire appliance?

parts.words: The driver of Blake's fire appliance?
parts.note: surface reading: whoever drives a fire engine belonging to someone called Blake

parts.words: The driver of Blake's fire appliance?
parts.note: setter's reading: Blake's hymn Jerusalem asks for a chariot of fire, so its driver is wanted

explanation.walkthrough: William Blake's poem Jerusalem says 'Bring me my chariot of fire'; a fire appliance is a British term for a fire engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A charioteer is the person who drives a chariot, here the burning vehicle of Blake's famous hymn.

clue.text: See 12

definitions.note: a pointer: the definition, Measure for Measure, is in the clue at 12

wordplay.note: the clue at 12, whose rearranged letters supply the middle of the saying

explanation.walkthrough: This light is the middle of 12-across: TWO CAN PLAY (12) AT THAT (14) GAME (11), an anagram of to placate my angst, What a, less S.
explanation.definitionFit: These two words sit in the middle of the proverb warning that a rival may retaliate in kind.

clue.text: An hour in the fashion editor's set up

indicators.note: an hour spent in something is held within it, so those letters sit inside the next piece

parts.note: ton, from French, is fashion or the fashionable set
hr is the abbreviation for hour
ed is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A fashion editor's photo shoot is arranged within an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' sounds like arranging a shoot, but it means raised to a seat of power, as a monarch is.
explanation.definitionFit: To be throned is to be placed on a throne, set up in a seat of royal authority.

clue.text: Arnold Bennett initially turned on Denry Machin: I find that rum!

indicators.note: turned means faced the other way, so those letters run backwards
initially points to the opening letters of the name

parts.note: the initials of the novelist
Denry Machin is the hero of Bennett's novel The Card
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reader finds it odd that Bennett turned on his own character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the British slang for odd, which is the surface's sense; it is the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacardi is a well-known brand of white rum, originally from Cuba, so it is an example of the spirit.

clue.text: Flourished as Leopold?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: thrived, came into flower

definitions.note: cryptic: made into Bloom, as if Bloom were a verb
definitions.meaning: second meaning: turned into Leopold Bloom, the hero of Joyce's Ulysses

explanation.walkthrough: Leopold Bloom is the central figure of James Joyce's Ulysses; the question mark flags treating his surname as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that have opened their flowers have thrived, and the word also jokingly means made into Joyce's hero.

clue.text: They stop the current flow of coppers retaining an informer

indicators.note: retaining means holding on to, so one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, made plural
a tout is slang for an informer

explanation.surface: Police officers who have an informant inside the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police, but it is the chemical element copper, twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut-outs are safety switches or fuses that break an electric circuit automatically when the load is too high.

clue.text: No backbone, naturally, in this poor wretch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a creature without a spine by nature, an invertebrate
second meaning: a contemptible, insignificant person

explanation.surface: A miserable person, lacking any courage by temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No backbone' sounds like a character flaw, but taken literally it describes an invertebrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects are invertebrates with no spine, and the word is also used scornfully for a worthless, despicable person.

clue.text: Warm drink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: friendly and sincere in manner
second meaning: a sweet fruit beverage or liqueur

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to heat up a beverage, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial describes a friendly, heartfelt welcome, and is also a concentrated fruit syrup diluted for drinking.

clue.text: Hope to stay in traction? Not with this treatment!

indicators.note: traction pulls and stretches the body, so these letters are pulled out of shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hospital patient hopes to stay strung up in traction, but is told this therapy works differently.
explanation.walkthrough: Traction is a hospital technique of pulling on limbs; the definition contrasts it with manipulation of the spine.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteopathy is a form of therapy that relieves pain by manipulating the bones, joints and muscles.

clue.text: See 24

definitions.note: a pointer: the definition, cheese, is in the clue at 24

wordplay.note: the clue at 24, where the rearranged scientist's name supplies these letters

explanation.walkthrough: This light completes 24-across: MO (doctor) plus Pasteur rearranged gives MOUSETRAP, slang for cheap cheese, split as MOUSE (24) and TRAP (21).
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a device for catching animals, and with the first half at 24 it names the cheap cheese used as bait.

clue.text: Religious representation from religious separatists

parts.note: pi is crossword slang for pious, religious
ETA was the Basque separatist group

explanation.surface: A sacred image produced by a breakaway religious sect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'religious' appears twice: the first is part of the definition, the second gives PI; ETA fought for Basque independence from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead body of Christ.

clue.text: Big fish in this

parts.note: surface reading: a large fish moves through some body of water
setter's reading: important people are in the thick of current affairs

explanation.walkthrough: A big fish is an important person; being in the swim means involved in the latest activity.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom in the swim means actively involved in fashionable events, where influential people are found.

clue.text: (and 21) Doctor Pasteur fermented cheese

definitions.note: defines the whole MOUSETRAP across 24 and 21

indicators.note: fermenting churns and transforms its contents, so the scientist's name is reworked
and 21 says the rest of the phrase continues in another light, so those closing letters leave this one

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
taken as written
the closing letters are entered at 21 instead of here

explanation.surface: Louis Pasteur, the scientist of fermentation, at work on some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer MOUSETRAP spans 24 and 21. Mousetrap is British slang for cheap, ordinary cheddar.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousetrap is a slang name for plain, low-quality cheese, the sort used to bait traps for rodents.

clue.text: As innocent as the two boys in green

definitions.meaning: second meaning: from the folk song Green Grow the Rushes, O, where two are the boys clothed all in green

explanation.surface: Two lads dressed in green are as innocent as can be.
explanation.walkthrough: The counting song Green Grow the Rushes, O has the line 'Two, two, the lily-white boys, clothed all in green-o'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lily-white means pure and blameless, after the white flower's traditional association with purity.

clue.text: What Shiva would do to some Franco-Hellenic battleground

parts.note: des is French for some
Troy was the site of the Greeks' war in Homer's Iliad

explanation.surface: The Hindu god's likely treatment of a Franco-Greek battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Franco-Hellenic' looks like one adjective; it splits into a French word and a Greek site.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu belief Shiva is the Destroyer within the trinity, alongside Brahma the creator and Vishnu the preserver.

clue.text: Barak's cover in the UK-Malay trouble

indicators.note: trouble is disorder and unrest, so the letters before it are thrown into disarray

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Israeli leader takes shelter during a diplomatic row between Britain and Malaysia.
explanation.walkthrough: Ehud Barak was Israeli prime minister when this was set; cover means headwear, not protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarmulke or yamulka is the skullcap worn by Jewish men, so it is the head covering of an Israeli.
